description: Image update proposals for the devinfra stack. Comments live in `description` fields
rather than in JSON5 comments so this file stays strict JSON and stdlib parsers can
read it; scripts/assert_renovate.py is one such parser and is what proves the regexes
below still match something. See docs/adr/0010-image-updates-are-proposed-by-regex-over-the-dotenv-template.md
for why neither the Compose manager nor Dependabot is an option here.
prHourlyLimit and prConcurrentLimit are 0 (unlimited) because the weekly schedule in
.github/workflows/renovate.yml is already the rate limit. Renovate's defaults of 2 and 10
would cap a run at two proposals; story 1.5 alone left four images behind, so the default
would silently withhold half of them and the repository would look more current than it is.
prBodyNotes: The README service table's Version column is **not** updated by this bot: it records abbreviated versions (`8.10`, `12.2`), so no regex can maintain it. Update the row for this image by hand before merging.

Merge only on a green CI run. `pixi run lint-pins` proves `.env.example` and the `compose.yaml` fallback moved together; the stack jobs prove the new image actually starts and passes the strict smoke suite.

description: Every pinned tag lives in two files that must move together: the annotated
`<NAME>_VERSION=` declaration in .env.example, and the `${<NAME>_VERSION:-tag}`
fallback in compose.yaml. Both are read by this single manager, so one image at
one version resolves to one branch — and therefore one pull request carrying both
edits. Split across two managers the extractions would still share a branch name,
but nothing would keep their versioning settings in step.
One image per pull request. Grouping would make a red run unattributable, which is
the whole reason this repository ships one commit per bump.
Silo publishes `RELEASE.<date>T<time>Z`, which docker versioning cannot order. The
annotation in .env.example carries the same `versioning=` value; this rule states it
again for the compose.yaml half of the pair, where there is no annotation to read.
Without it the two extractions would disagree about what `newValue` is and the bot
would edit one file alone — which lint-pins rejects.
